# SQL table functions with scalar parameters and optional explicit return schemas.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/table-functions.md
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language.md

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FUNCTION scalars.tvf_filter(lower_bound INT64) AS (SELECT a FROM scalars.t WHERE a > lower_bound);
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scalars.tvf_filter(2)
=> "1"

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FUNCTION scalars.tvf_null(x INT64) AS (SELECT x AS y);
SELECT y FROM scalars.tvf_null(NULL)
=> null

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FUNCTION scalars.tvf_explicit(x INT64) RETURNS TABLE<y FLOAT64> AS (SELECT x AS y);
SELECT TYPEOF(y) FROM scalars.tvf_explicit(1)
=> "FLOAT64"

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FUNCTION scalars.tvf_array(x ARRAY<STRING>) AS (SELECT ARRAY_LENGTH(x) AS y);
SELECT y FROM scalars.tvf_array(['a', 'b'])
=> "2"

# As documented, a column takes precedence over a table-function parameter of the same name.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FUNCTION scalars.tvf_shadow(a INT64) AS (SELECT a FROM scalars.t WHERE a > a);
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scalars.tvf_shadow(0)
=> "0"

# View columns, like table columns, are case-insensitive identifiers.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scalars.view_column_case AS SELECT 1 AS MixedCase;
SELECT mixedcase FROM scalars.view_column_case
=> "1"
